column1: # A line with a real reason to break one says "lesson-ok: <id>" in a comment. Add a row with each lesson that a pattern can catch.

column4: Tests never wait for a length of time: wait on a latch, future, listener, FxWait or the code's flush() (src/test/CLAUDE.md).
No timeout of a test's own: JUnit's global timeout is the only limit; wait on what the code does (src/test/CLAUDE.md).
The language changes live (UnichatApp.relocalize): a text kept in a static final stays in the old language. Call I18n.t where it is shown.
JavaFX animates a GIF in new Image() forever and keeps every frame (OOM in a day): use AnimatedImage.decodeGif / still.
A looked-up color derived from itself is a loop: compute it in code (Theme.accessibleAccent).
Author CSS beats setMinWidth(USE_PREF_SIZE): a min width in CSS truncated wide glyphs to "". Set it in code.
A file from other people goes to ffmpeg through Ffmpeg.input: it also refuses playlists and manifests that make ffmpeg read other local files.
The state a browser sign-in gets back is compared in constant time (Loopback.ours, MessageDigest.isEqual): equals stops at the first different character.
One HttpClient per class (a static, or a field when its settings differ), never one per call: each keeps its own threads and connections until it is collected.

CompletableFuture.join() ignores JUnit's global timeout (it can't be interrupted): a future that never completes hangs the build for good instead of failing. Use get(); a Thread's join() is fine (lesson-ok).

A program is run through support/Processes (capture with a Limit and input): ReplyWriter, Transcriber and CloakJob each ran their own, and interrupting their thread left the program and its children running.
